clue.text: Weigh down our retreat, carrying tote, sack, or bundle, e.g.

indicators.note: one thing carrying another holds it inside, so the first piece wraps around the second

blocks.note: our + den, a den being a retreat or hideaway
tote, sack and bundle are all examples of verbs

explanation.surface: Someone loads up a hideaway with bags and bundles until it is weighed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of carrying words looks like part of the picture, but 'e.g.' turns them into examples of a part of speech: VERB goes inside OUR DEN to give OVERBURDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To overburden is to load with too much, a synonym for weighing someone or something down.

clue.text: Speaker's frequently murdered

indicators.note: a speaker's version is the word as said, not as written

blocks.note: oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A politician keeps getting killed in his speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: Offed is slang, mainly American, for killed; said aloud the ending is swallowed and it sounds like oft.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is slang for to kill them, so offed is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: How to get silence from Western lawman and galoot

blocks.note: Wyatt Earp, the Wild West marshal
a lug is a clumsy oaf, as is a galoot

explanation.surface: A cowboy story's sheriff and a big oaf are the means of quieting a room.
explanation.walkthrough: Wyatt Earp was the lawman of the Tombstone gunfight; galoot and lug are both American words for a big clumsy man.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug blocks sound from reaching the ear, a practical way to obtain quiet.

clue.text: Comedy duo to incinerate footwear over most of penitential period

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter

blocks.note: to incinerate is to burn
a sandal is an open shoe
Lent is the season of penance before Easter

explanation.surface: A double act's routine about burning shoes during the season of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: George Burns and Gracie Allen were an American husband-and-wife double act of radio and TV. 'Over' only stacks the pieces in order in a down entry; Lent is the forty days before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns and Allen were a famous vaudeville, radio and television double act, so they are a comedy pair.

clue.text: Destroyed their coral, expecting no response

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: People wreck their reef and do not wait for anyone to object.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical question is asked for effect, with no reply anticipated.

clue.text: Excellent No. 1 weapon

blocks.note: E stands for excellent in some grading scales
number one is a child's word for urinating

explanation.surface: A first-rate top-ranked fencing sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 1 weapon' reads as the best sword, but number one is nursery talk for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Experts with permission to enter after removing duplicates

indicators.note: any letter that appears twice in a row loses its second copy, shortening the word

blocks.note: access is the right to go in

explanation.surface: Specialists are let into a building once the duplicate passes have been weeded out.
explanation.walkthrough: ACCESS has a doubled C and a doubled S; dropping one of each leaves ACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are people who are highly skilled at something, so the plural noun matches experts.

clue.text: Revolutionary sale disrupted Manhattan neighborhood

indicators.note: a disrupted order is thrown into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Protesters break up a store sale in a part of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a district on the west side of Manhattan, an area of New York City.

clue.text: Poor sci-fi novel is sleep-inducing

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: A weak science-fiction book puts its readers to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the noun for the book itself, but it is the adjective new, signalling a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: Soporific describes something that causes drowsiness, like a dull book or a sedative.

clue.text: Listening to Hitler in anger

indicators.note: we are told to attend to how a word is heard rather than how it is written

blocks.note: Hitler's title, the Führer, said out loud

explanation.surface: Hearing a dictator speak makes a listener seethe.
explanation.walkthrough: FUROR is the American spelling of furore, and its sound matches Führer, the title Hitler took.
explanation.definitionFit: A furor is an outburst of rage or public outrage, close in sense to anger.

clue.text: I can mug loudly for cosmetic products

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so what matters is how the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: can means may (be allowed to) and a mug is a cup

explanation.surface: Someone boasts noisily that they can rob people to get their cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' suggests robbery, but here it is a noun turned into a cup: 'I may cup', said aloud, runs together into EYE MAKEUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye makeup covers mascara, eyeliner and eyeshadow, all kinds of cosmetic products.

clue.text: Libertarian fantasy, ultimately: not winding up quiet and stalwart

indicators.note: not reaching the finish means the final letter is left off

blocks.note: at last means ultimately
sh is a call for quiet
rugged means sturdy and tough

explanation.surface: A dream of a free society that, in the end, does not wind up quiet and solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' looks like it takes a last letter, but it is AT LAST, which loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas Shrugged is Ayn Rand's novel, a utopian fiction beloved of libertarians.

clue.text: Unsoiled? Ridiculous misconception

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurdly out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters

explanation.surface: Believing something can stay perfectly clean is a silly mistaken idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A delusion is a false belief firmly held, which is a kind of misconception.

clue.text: After mediocre grade, failure is not so far off

indicators.note: one piece follows another, so they are placed in that order

blocks.note: a C is an average school mark
a loser is a person who fails

explanation.surface: A student who got a middling mark is nearly failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer is the comparative of close, meaning nearer, or less distant.

clue.text: Nary a buck is raised to shelter a grumbler

indicators.note: lifted up in a down entry, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a clam is slang for a dollar, so no clam means not a single buck
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Not a dollar is collected to house a complainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Clams is American slang for dollars. NO CLAM read upwards gives MALCON, and TENT completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a person dissatisfied with things who habitually complains.

clue.text: Countryman caught in a rainstorm

indicators.note: something caught in something else is trapped inside it
a storm throws things about, so the letters before it are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: one printed word doing two jobs: its first part is the definition and its last three letters are the next piece
a gent is a gentleman
one printed word doing two jobs: its first part is fodder and its end is the scrambling signal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rural fellow gets drenched in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' reads as one word for a rustic, but it splits: Country is the definition and man the gent who is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Lee dominates small and mischievous aquarium dweller

indicators.note: in a down entry, to dominate is to sit above, so the first piece goes on top

blocks.note: Ang Lee, the film director
elfish means impish, like a small elf

explanation.surface: A man called Lee lords it over a tiny troublemaker in a fish tank.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee stands for its partner name: the director Ang Lee. ANG sits above ELFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelfish are popular tropical fish kept in home tanks, so one lives in an aquarium.

clue.text: Devour accessory

blocks.note: first meaning: to eat greedily, a slang verb
second meaning: a piece of cloth worn around the neck

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a strange instruction to eat an accomplice; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarf food is to wolf it down, and a scarf is also a neck wrap worn as a fashion item.

clue.text: Stream magazine keeping back letter from Athens

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the letters within itself, inside the run of words
read backwards, from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A river magazine holds back a letter sent from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'streAM MAGazine'; read backwards they give GAMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third character of the Greek alphabet, and Athens is the Greek capital.

clue.text: Aware of a bit of murky fluid swirling around pole

indicators.note: just a small piece, the opening letter of the next word
swirling stirs things round, so the letters get mixed
the mixed letters go round the outside of the next piece

blocks.note: the first letter of murky
taken as written
N for north, a pole

explanation.surface: Someone notices murky liquid eddying round a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a stick, but it is one of the compass poles, giving N.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindful of something means conscious of it or attentive to it, the same sense as aware of.

clue.text: One who drinks a lot of brewed cocoa? I'll set about heating at first

indicators.note: brewing stirs ingredients together, so the letters are mixed up
to be set about something is to be placed around it, so the mixed letters wrap the next piece
only the opening letter of the word before is used

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written without the apostrophe
the initial of heating

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker of hot chocolate promises to start warming the next mugful.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that drinking lots of cocoa does not really make someone an alcoholic; that drink is only the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic is a person dependent on liquor, someone who habitually drinks heavily.

clue.text: Loss of oil, perhaps, in the era of kale salad?

indicators.note: a salad is a mix of things tossed together, so the letters are tossed

blocks.note: letters tossed
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Wondering whether oil spills are a sign of our trendy kale-eating times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kale salad' reads as a dish, but salad tells us to toss the letters of kale; the era follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the escape of fluid from a container, and an oil spill is one instance.

clue.text: Solitary military officer lacks company? Yes

indicators.note: something that lacks a part is missing it, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a colonel is a senior army officer
Co. is the standard abbreviation of company
Y is short for yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: A lone colonel, asked whether he has no companions, answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: COLONEL without its CO leaves LONEL; adding Y for yes completes LONELY. The question and answer also confirm that a lonely person lacks company.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely can describe something isolated or standing alone, so it can stand in for solitary.

clue.text: Shield is put down when holding a lance's end

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside, so a letter goes within
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: to put someone down is to belittle them
taken as written
the last letter of lance

explanation.surface: A knight's shield is lowered while it grips the tip of a lance.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside INSULT, then the E that ends lance is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To insulate is to protect or cut off from outside influence, as a verb meaning shield.

clue.text: Internet hosting entails a distinctive set of beliefs and practices

definitions.text: a distinctive set of beliefs and practices

indicators.note: to host is to contain a guest, so the answer is held within the words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Running websites comes with its own culture and code of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosting' is web-site hosting in the surface, but it also holds the answer: interNET HOSting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit and values of a group or culture.

clue.text: Mine a kind of bread

blocks.note: a pit is a mine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim of ownership over a particular loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive, but it is the noun, a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pita is a flat Middle Eastern bread, one type of bread.

clue.text: Childish member of a social group breaking in tool

indicators.note: one thing breaking another bursts into the middle of it

blocks.note: taken as written
a file is a tool for smoothing
ants are social insects living in colonies

explanation.surface: An immature member of a club breaks in a new tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social group' suggests a club or clique, but the member is an insect: ants are social insects living in organized colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile means like a baby or immature, a stronger synonym of childish.

clue.text: Chart of gangsta hip-hop hits

blocks.note: the initial of gangsta
rap is hip-hop music
H is the abbreviation for hits in a baseball box score

explanation.surface: A list ranking the best-selling gangsta rap songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chart of hits' paints a music chart, but the definition is a diagram. H for hits is a baseball scoring convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram of data, a kind of chart.

clue.text: Start to haul ancient part of a boat

indicators.note: 'Start to' keeps only the first letter of 'haul'

blocks.note: the first letter of haul
ancient means very old

explanation.surface: Begin dragging a very old section of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The hold is the cargo space below a ship's deck, one section of the vessel.

clue.text: Pretentious dancer originally coming inside to iron fancy garment

indicators.note: at its origin, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept
the pieces before it go into the middle of the next word

blocks.note: arty means affectedly artistic
originally takes the first letter of dancer
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A showy dancer arrives to press an elaborate outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A party dress is a smart frock worn for a celebration, a fancy item of clothing.
